note: Round trip 6's prediction table, written BEFORE the editor ran. Every row states a probe, the hypotheses that compete over it, and which one this table predicts. read.ts resolves the probe on the build and on the export and reports which hypotheses survive: exactly one -> CONFIRMED or REFUTED, more than one -> AMBIGUOUS (the rig cannot separate them), none -> REFUTED, nothing on the table predicted it. basis: doc = an official Spine page, inferred = a prior measurement with its issue, none = no basis at all, which is the point of the row.

bases.doc-nonessential: https://esotericsoftware.com/spine-json-format and https://esotericsoftware.com/spine-export -- data marked nonessential is only written when the Nonessential data export box is checked, and that list is: the skeleton's fps, images and audio; a mesh's and a linked mesh's width and height; a mesh's edges; and the editor colours of bounding box, path, point and clipping attachments. Quoted in docs/AUTHORING.md 10.5.
bases.doc-defaults: https://esotericsoftware.com/spine-json-format -- the exporter omits a field equal to its default, which is why the format page is a list of assume-N-if-omitted. Quoted in docs/AUTHORING.md 10.5.
bases.doc-boundingbox: https://esotericsoftware.com/spine-bounding-boxes -- bounding boxes are an editor feature with their own attachment type.
bases.doc-clipping: https://esotericsoftware.com/spine-clipping -- clipping attachments are an editor feature, and the end slot is part of the documented model.
bases.doc-transform: https://esotericsoftware.com/spine-transform-constraints -- transform constraints are an editor feature.
bases.doc-path: https://esotericsoftware.com/spine-path-constraints -- position, spacing and rotate modes are the documented model.
bases.doc-shear: https://esotericsoftware.com/spine-keys -- shear is a keyable bone property.
bases.doc-draworder: https://esotericsoftware.com/spine-slots and https://esotericsoftware.com/spine-keys -- the draw order can be keyed, and offsets count from the setup order.
bases.doc-blend: https://esotericsoftware.com/spine-slots -- a slot carries a blend mode and a two-colour tint.
bases.doc-images: https://esotericsoftware.com/spine-images -- the editor finds an image by appending the attachment name to the Images path, unless the attachment has a Path.
bases.m-535: issue #535 -- the editor returned bones, slots and constraints element for element, and re-keyed every name-keyed object.
bases.m-539: issue #539 -- the re-key is natural order, case-insensitive; events are re-keyed and their firings still resolve by name.
bases.m-540: issue #540 -- twelve physics constraints, x and y kept, rotate/scaleX/shearX discarded, and every constraint's strength returned exactly.
bases.m-541: issue #541 and PR #552 -- skins is re-sorted with default pinned first.
bases.m-368: issue #368 -- the editor recomputes a mesh hull and drops internal edges on import, warning that Nonessential was unchecked.
bases.m-369: issue #369 -- a curve over a hold segment comes back stepped.
bases.m-370: issue #370 -- skeleton.images is resolved against the skeleton's directory and re-anchored on export; the editor collapses ./ to no path.

rows.question: does the editor recompute the mesh hull, as issue #368 measured it doing to authored meshes
rows.basisNote: m-368 -- on the pass-1 trip every authored mesh came back with every vertex a hull vertex. This mesh has FIVE vertices and a hull of four, chosen so the two answers cannot coincide: a keep reads 4 and a recompute reads 5. An earlier draft of this rig used a bare quad, where hull already equalled the vertex count, and the reader printed AMBIGUOUS on it -- which is what the rig deserved.
